name: Mandaya
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Estrera, Edward G. 2020. A Grammatical Sketch of Mandaya (56 pp; in Glottolog hh bibliography, no online copy found); also Gallman 1983 Proto East Mindanao (comparative, incl. accent)
earlier_scan.note: Zorc 1977 (PL C-44, read) cites Mandayan forms with accent marks in comparative sets but gives no Mandaya stress statement

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Mandaya language' (raw wikitext, 2026-09-17), phonology tables citing Estrera 2020
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Vowel and consonant tables and one allophony note attributed to Estrera 2020; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Duping, Arnold M. 2021. Phonological variations among Mandaya dialects: a multiple case study. International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science 5(12): 380-386. DOI 10.47772/ijriss.2021.51221
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phoneme inventory (17 C, 6 V incl. schwa) for Cateel, Caraga, Manay, Tarragona Mandaya. Never uses the word stress; Table 5 (p. 384) presents 'vowel lengthening' of /a:/ /u:/ (/i:/, /ə:/) as 'another distinct characteristic of Mandaya phonology', with length on the penult in /bu:yak/ 'flower', /katu:mbal/ 'chili', /sə:psəp/, but on the antepenult in /i:yayas/ 'wild pig', /magai:kol/ 'laugh'; no rule for its placement is given and it is not related to stress.

sources.citation: Galvez, Lilibeth S. 2018. Isogloss of Mandaya lexemes: looking into their linguistic variations. Davao Research Journal 12(1): 27-43. DOI 10.59120/drj.v12i1.11
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lexical isoglosses across Mati, Tarragona, Manay, Caraga, Baganga, Cateel, Boston; mentions 'vowel lengthening in the first syllable' for individual lexemes (hapon, ani) as a dialect difference; no stress rule.

sources.citation: Pasion, Raymund M. & Mary Ann S. Sandoval. 2013. Varyasyong ponolohikal ng wikang Mandaya sa ilang munisipalidad ng Davao Oriental. Davao Research Journal 9(1): 56-66. DOI 10.59120/drj.v9i1.30
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: In Filipino. Segmental variation only (/h/ loss in Caraga/Manay, schwa and glide l retention). p. 65 Rekomendasyon 1 calls for a future study 'batay sa ponemang suprasegmental: tono, haba, diin at antala' (tone, length, stress, juncture) — i.e. stress is explicitly not treated.

sources.citation: Gallman, Andrew F. 1979. Proto-South-East Mindanao and its internal relationships. In A. Gallman, E. J. Allison, C. W. Harmon & J. Witucki (eds.), Papers in Philippine Linguistics No. 10, 1-52. Pacific Linguistics A-55. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A55.1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.1 (pp. 6-8) gives consonant and vowel correspondence sets for five Mandayan wordlists (Islam, Maragusan, Kabasagan, Caraga, Boso) but nothing on stress or accent; p. 6 states 'There is no complete phonemic statement available for any of SEM languages except KLT and MSK' and that the Mandayan lists are unanalysed dialect-survey lists. The only stress sentence in the volume (p. 135) is Witucki's on Chamorro.

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1977. The Bisayan dialects of the Philippines: subgrouping and reconstruction. Pacific Linguistics C-44. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5629 .Z6
sources.note: Sec. 8.10 (p. 217) on Proto-Bisayan accent: 'Mansaka and Kalagan.. exhibit a complementary phenomenon of phonemic shortness (in Mansaka) and phonemic length (in Kalagan) which coincides with Bs and Tg accent patterns.. these forms are only remnants of a pre-existing system since many forms are unmarked for accent'. Sister languages only; nothing on Mandaya itself.
